Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are making their way out in the middle now. The two openers for India are Ishan Kishan and Shubman Gill. Jacob Duffy to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, New Zealand have posted a well below-par total on the board and it is a daunting task for them to defend this one. India, on the other hand will feel quite confident of gunning this down and this will also give their top order to get some runs under their belt as they can play without much pressure. Let's see how things pan out in the second innings.

India would be very pleased with their bowling effort, and their decision to include an extra spinner worked wonders for them. It all started with a wicket-maiden first over from Yuzvendra Chahal, and after that, they did not let the Kiwi batters settle in. They kept taking wickets at regular intervals and did not give away any loose deliveries. The fielding was on point as well, as they backed their bowlers well. Arshdeep Singh was the pick of the bowlers with two wickets and conceding just seven runs in his two overs. This is what cricket is all about as in one game you may go for runs, but in the next game you can be the hero as well. Every bowler except for Shivam Mavi who came into the attack got into the wickets column. Now, it is upto their batters to finish the job and level the series.

The decision to bat first backfired massively for New Zealand. The struggle against spin for the Kiwi batters was quite prominent in their batting display here. They could not read the spinners and opted for some poor shots throughout the innings. New Zealand could not build any partnerships in the middle, which they did in the first game. Also, losing four wickets to reverse-sweeps did not help them much. Mitchell Santner was their top-scorer with 19 runs and no other batter could cross 15 runs which tells the story of this innings.

A dominant display of bowling from India! This has been a special effort from the Men in Blue, especially in such a crucial game. They were all over New Zealand right from the start and never let their foot off the gas. The Kiwis will need to erase this from their memories quickly and focus on the areas that they need to work on. This is also the lowest total for New Zealand against India in T20Is.

LEG BYE! Very full and at the toes, Mitchell Santner backs away and swings hard at it but fails to connect yet again. The ball deflects off the pads onto the off side and they scamper through for a leg bye. New Zealand finish with 99/8 on the board, their lowest T20I score against India.
Three dots on the trot now! Another short ball over the stumps, Mitchell Santner walks towards the ball and looks to muscle it away but is well beaten.
Mitchell Santner shuffles past the leg stump and Arshdeep Singh follows him yet again with a fuller delivery. Santner looks to carve it away but misses.
This is banged in short and around off middle, Mitchell Santner looks to take on the pull shot but the ball climbs on the batter and beats the bat as well.
Two more! This is full and following the batter past the leg stump, Mitchell Santner miscues it toward square leg and does well to come back for the second run.
This is full and at the toes, Mitchell Santner does well to clip it away in front of deep mid-wicket and he races back for the second.
Gets it in the blockhole around leg stump, Mitchell Santner jams it off the inside edge and down to fine leg for a single. Can he take New Zealand to over the 100-run mark now?
Who will bowl the last over? It will be Arshdeep Singh (1-0-3-2).
WIDE! This is full and well down the leg side, Mitchell Santner misses the flick and a wide is called.
Full and straight, this has been driven down to long on for a single.
WIDE! An attempted slower bouncer outside off but it is called a wide for height.
A low full toss on the legs, Mitchell Santner clips it to deep backward square leg for a run.
This is short and wide, Jacob Duffy bends his back and lifts it over the cover region for a single.
FOUR! Muscled away! Shivam Mavi bangs this one in short and over middle, Jacob Duffy is able to free his arms and pulls it in front of square on the leg side for a boundary.
This is pitched up around off stump, Mitchell Santner pushes it toward mid off and picks up a single.
Jacob Duffy is the new man in. Also, Shivam Mavi to bowl the penultimate over.

OUT! CAUGHT! That could have been ugly but Arshdeep Singh gets his second wicket. This is served on a shorter length again from over the wicket. The ball is well directed and at the body, cramping Lockie Ferguson for room. Ferguson looks to awkwardly fend it away but only manages to get a glove on it. The ball ops up around the gully region with the keeper and the fielder at point both going for it. In the end, Ishan Kishan pulls out and Washington Sundar takes a simple catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Washington Sundar b Arshdeep Singh

Commentary.Commentary: Back to around the wicket and this is full and at the legs, Lockie Ferguson flicks it straight to mid-wicket.
Lockie Ferguson comes out to the middle now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Arshdeep Singh picks up a wicket now. This is banged in short and over middle, hurrying on the batter. Ish Sodhi backs away and throws his bat at it. The ball takes the higher part of the bat and lobs up around mid on where Hardik Pandya takes a simple catch and returns the favour back to Arshdeep from the previous over. New Zealand struggling to get to even 100 here.
Commentary.Howout: c Hardik Pandya b Arshdeep Singh

Commentary.Commentary: This is full and angling at the toes, Mitchell Santner backs away and flicks it well in front of mid-wicket for just another single. Boundaries are at a premium here!
Comes from around the wicket now and serves a slower one around off. Ish Sodhi waits forit and dabs it down to third man for a run.
Shorter one on the body, Mitchell Santner works it off his hips down to fine leg for a single.
Ish Sodhi walks out to bat now. Also, Arshdeep Singh bowling his first over of the match.

OUT! CAUGHT! Smart catch from Arshdeep Singh in the deep and Michael Bracewell has to depart. Hardik Pandya bangs in a good bumper around the body and gets it around shoulder height. Bracewell takes it on and gets it off the top edge toward the fine leg fence. Arshdeep there walks back and takes it reverse cup over his head and just as he is about to lose control, he flicks the ball back in the air and comes back inside to complete the catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Arshdeep Singh b Hardik Pandya

Commentary.Commentary: Is that a clean catch? Arshdeep Singh takes a good catch in the deep, but as he moves over the boundary ropes he lifts up the ball in the air and pouches it safely after coming inside. The replay shows that it is a clean catch and Michael Bracewell has to go.
This is very full and around leg stump, Michael Bracewell looks to stay deep and slog it away but misses. The ball hits the pads and lobs to the right of the bowler.
Full and following the batter down the leg side, Mitchell Santner clips it uppishly toward deep mid-wicket and picks up yet another single.
Back of a length around leg stump, Michael Bracewell looks to pull it away but mistimes it badly toward leg gully. They scamper through for one.
Good length around middle and leg, this is worked away in front of mid-wicket for a run.
This is short and on the body, Michael Bracewell pulls it behind square on the leg side for a single.
This is held back a touch and bowled on a length around middle, Mitchell Santner fends it back onto the deck.
Make that five! Flatter one around off, Michael Bracewell forces it off the back foot toward wide long off for another single.
Four singles in a row now! This is tossed up full and on middle, Santner drives it through extra cover for a single.
This is shorter and outside off, Michael Bracewell cuts it off the back foot to sweeper cover and rotates the strike.
Floated up on off stump, Mitchell Santner plays an uppish drive down to long off for one more.
Kuldeep Yadav comes back in for his final over and starts off with a flatter delivery around off. Michael Bracewell plays it off the back foot through covers for one.
This is on a hard length and on the sixth stump line, Mitchell Santner looks to play at it, but gets beaten on the outside edge.
A yorker now, on off, Michael Bracewell digs it out towards long off for one.
Back of a length and on leg, Mitchell Santner nudges it towards deep backward sqaure leg for a run.
Goes fuller and on leg, Michael Bracewell flicks it through square leg for a single.
Length again and on off, Michael Bracewell pushes it towards covers.

This is on a good length and around off, nips back in, Michael Bracewell looks to work it away, but misses and gets hit on the pads as the ball goes towards the keeper. There is a stiffled appeal, but turned down.
Hardik Pandya bangs this short seeing the batter adavnce down the track, Michael Bracewell though lets it go to the keeper as it is way over his head height. It is called a wide.
Hardik Pandya (2-0-17-0) brings himself back into the attack.
Quicker one, full and on off, Mitchell Santner pushes it towards covers.
Angles this one into the batter, on leg, Mitchell Santner knocks it to the right of the bowler.
Slower through the air, on off, Mitchell Santner steers it towards point.
FOUR! Classic shot! This is tossed up, full and on off, Mitchell Santner carves it through covers for a boundary.
Floated, short and on off, turning away, Michael Bracewell forces it towards extra covers where Hardik Pandya manages to get a hand to it. They cross.
Flighted, full and on off, Michael Bracewell blocks it out.
Washington Sundar (2-0-12-1) is back on.
A single to end the over as this full delivery is drilled towards long on.
Floated, full and on off, Mitchell Santner drives it towards long off for one.
The Kiwi skipper, Mitchell Santner walks out to bat with his team in a spot of real bother.

OUT! RUN OUT! A disaster for New Zealand! Lack of communication cost the Kiwis here. Deepak Hooda floats this up, full and on middle, Mark Chapman goes for the reverse sweep, but gets a top edge towards short fine leg. Kuldeep Yadav is in two minds whether to go for the catch or not and falls over as the ball drops in front of him. Chapman though sets off for the run and is halfway through, Bracewell takes a couple of steps forward but sends his partner back. Kuldeep collects and throws it towards the keeper's end where Ishan Kishan does the rest with Chapman nowhere near the crease. New Zealand lose half their side now.
Short again and on off, Mark Chapman moves back, but slices it straight to point.
Shortish and outside off, Michael Bracewell cuts it through point for a run.
Tossed up, full and on middle, Mark Chapman sweeps it of the outer half towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Deepak Hooda (3-0-13-1) to finish off his spell here.
A bit short and on middle, turning away, Michael Bracewell defends it off the back foot towards the bowler.
Tossed up, on middle, Mark Chapman uses his feet and drills it towards long on for one more.
Looped up, full and on leg, Michael Bracewell eases it towards long on for one.
Floated, full and on middle, Michael Bracewell knocks it towards short covers.
Quicker, full and on leg, Mark Chapman goes on his back foot to play at it, but gets an inside edge towards fine leg for a run.
Tossed up, full and on middle, Michael Bracewell clips it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

Washington Sundar is back on the field and is back into the attack as well but the umpire isn't allowing him to bowl straightaway as there is a rule stating the player needs to be on the field for a minimum of 8 minutes before coming back onto bowl. Kuldeep Yadav (2-0-8-1) to continue...
Darts this one full and on leg, Michael Bracewell tucks it towards square leg for one more.
Pushed through quciker, on off, Michael Bracewell blocks it down the pitch.
Tossed up, full and on middle, Mark Chapman sweeps it towards deep backward square leg for one.
Flatter and short, on off, Mark Chapman moves back and cuts it wide of deep point for a brace.
Short again and on middle, Michael Bracewell flicks it through square leg for a run.
Floated, short and on off, Mark Chapman lobs it towards long off for a single.

Drinks! Just as New Zealand were looking to be settling in, Kuldeep Yadav gets rid of Daryl Mitchell just before drinks. Indian spinners are all over the Kiwi batters here and they will look to wrap things up quickly. New Zealand knows that they need a partnership and anything around 140-150 will make a game out of this. An exciting second phase of this innings awaits us. Also, Michael Bracewell is the next man in for New Zealand.

OUT! TIMBER! A cracker-jack of a delivery from Kuldeep Yadav and Daryl Mitchell has to walk back as well. Quicker through the air and on a nagging length outside off. Mitchell goes on the back foot looking to punch it through covers but the ball grips and turns in a mile off the deck. Mitchell is beaten on the inside edge and the ball castles into the stumps. New Zealand lose their 4th wicket with only halfway through their full quota of overs.
This is looped up a bit and bowled very full on leg stump. Daryl Mitchell pushes it to the right of the bowler but Kuldeep Yadav makes a good diving stop.
Nicely tossed up on off stump, Daryl Mitchell blocks it off the front foot.
Shorter one, turning away from off stump, Mark Chapman backs away and punches it down to long off for one more.
Just milking the singles at the moment New Zealand. This is on a nagging length on the pads, Daryl Mitchell goes deep in his crease and tucks it to deep square leg for one.
This is very full and down the leg side, Mark Chapman works it behind square leg for a single.
On a length and on off stump, Daryl Mitchell uses his feet and just pushes it down to the left of long on for a couple of runs.
This is quicker and around off stump, Daryl Mitchell defends it back to the bowler.
Flatter one around off, this is tapped away in front of covers for a single.
Floated up around middle, Mark Chapman reaches forward to make the block.
This is fuller and on off stump, Daryl Mitchell gets inside the line and paddles it down to deep backward square leg for one more.
This is shorter and around off, Mark Chapman backs away and slaps it toward sweeper cover for a single.
Slight halt! It looks like Washington Sundar has done his webbing on his fingers. The physio is in to check on him, but unfortunately he is going out of the field now.

Today marks a historic day in Indian Women's cricket! The news from South Africa is that the India Under-19 Women's team have won the inaugral U-19 Women's T20 World Cup beating England in the final by 7 wickets.
Quicker one around off, this is pushed away toward cover.
FOUR! This is dragged down on off stump, Daryl Mitchell rocks back and pulls it in front of mid-wicket for a much-needed boundary.
This is around off, Mitchell comes forward again and pushes it back to the bowler.
Tossed up at the stumps, Daryl Mitchell steps out but ends up defending it.
Fuller and around off, Daryl Mitchell reaches forward and gets a leading edge toward square leg. They don't take the run.
Starts off with a flatter delivery on off stump, Mark Chapman rocks back and taps it through cover-point for one.
Kuldeep Yadav has been introduced into the attack now.
Flighted delivery, on a length and turning into the off stump, Daryl Mitchell blocks it out. Just 2 runs and a wicket off Hooda's first over.
Daryl Mitchell comes out to the middle now with New Zealand in a spot of bother.

OUT! TIMBER! Poor choice of shot from Glenn Phillips on this pitch and in such a situation as well. Deepak Hooda bowls this one quicker at 94.1 clicks and Phillips pre-meditates with the reverse paddle. All three stumps are exposed and Hooda fires it onto middle. This ons goes straight on and beats the bat, crashing into the stumps. New Zealand lose their third wicket and are in a spot of real bother here.

Flighted on a length around off and turning away, Mark Chapman taps it with the turn toward backward point for the quick single. The fielder there fires in a throw at the keeper's end and Ishan Kishan whips off the bails. The third umpire is called in and the replays show that Phillips had even crossed the stumps.
This is drifted onto leg stump, Glenn Phillips shuffles and nudges it leg side for a run.
Holds it back a touch and drifts it in from around off, Glenn Phillips stays solid in defense.
Starts off with fullish delivery angling in from outside off. Glenn Phillips defends it toward covers.
Deepak Hooda comes into the attack now.
This is a tad shorter around leg stump, Mark Chapman goes deep in his crease and works it to mid-wicket.
Half an appeal from the bowler for LBW but there seems to be a big inside edge. This is quicker and flatter on off stump, Glenn Phillips gets an inside edge toward square leg and picks up a single.
First runs off the bat for the Kiwis against Yuzvendra Chahal. This is short and outside off, Phillips cuts it through point for a couple of runs.
Yet another dot ball! This is pushed through on off stump, Glenn Phillips pushes it out toward cover.
A bit quicker now on off stump and turning away, Glenn Phillips goes on the back foot and manages to keep it out.
Flatter on middle and turning away, Glenn Phillips defends it off the front foot.
WIDE! This is floated up full but down the leg side, wide called.
Yuzvendra Chahal to continue...
Tossed up, full and on middle, Mark Chapman reverse sweeps it straight to point.
Short and on middle, turning in, Glenn Phillips nudges it towards short fine leg for a single and gets off the mark.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Washington Sundar strikes now! Indian spinners are all over the Kiwis here. This is a prized scalp as the in-form, Devon Conway goes back to the hut now. Sundar flights this up, full and on off, Devon Conway goes for the reverse-sweep, but the ball just lobs up off his gloves as Ishan Kishan takes a dolly behind the stumps. There is a huge appeal, and up goes the finger. Devon Conway reviews it straightaway. However, UltraEdge confirms that it has hit the gloves and New Zealand lose their second wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Ishan Kishan b Washington Sundar

Commentary.Commentary: Glenn Phillips is the new man in.

FIVE WIDES! Washington Sundar bowls this flatter and down the leg side, Devon Conway misses his flick and Ishan Kishan behind the stumps fails to stop it as well and the ball races to the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Quicker, full and of, Mark Chapman looks to sweep, but gets an inside edge towards short fine leg. They cross.

Run out chance.....missed! This is floated, full and on middle, Devon Conway looks to sweep it away, but mistimes it towards square leg. The batters sets off for the run as Ishan Kishan runs and has throws it at the batters end, but it needed to be better.
Shortish and on middle, Devon Conway pushes it towards mid on.
Washington Sundar (1-0-4-0) switches ends now.
A wicket-maiden over! This is short and on off, Mark Chapman blocks it out. Yuzvendra Chahal with a dream start here.

A huge appeal from India, but nothing doing! This is floated, full and on off, Mark Chapman looks to sweep, but misses as the ball goes off his pads and loops up. The fielder at first slip pouches it and they appeal, but the finger stays down.
Flighted, full and on off, Mark Chapman defends it onto his boot and the ball goes back to the bowler.
Mark Chapman is in at number 3.

OUT! DRAGGED ON! Yuzvendra Chahal draws first blood! The bowling change has worked for India and Finn Allen goes back to the hut. Chahal bowls this quicket and flatter around off, Finn Allen goes for the reverse-sweep, but misses and the ball goes off his back leg and crashes onto the stumps. A huge wicket for India and Chahal is delighted.
Floated, full and on middle, Finn Allen pushes it back towards the bowler.
Oh wow! What a delivery first up! Yuzvendra Chahal starts with a tossed up delivery, pitches on the leg stumps line, turns away outside off, Finn Allen gets beaten all ends up.
Yuzvendra Chahal comes in to replace Washington Sundar.
Goes fuller and on middle, swinging in, Finn Allen uses his feet, but gets cramped for room and mistimes his drive towards mid on. They cross.
Back of a length and on middle, nips away a bit, Finn Allen gets squared up and gets hit high on his body as the ball rolls to the off side.
A touch fuller and outside off, Devon Conway guides it towards third man for a run.
On a length and on off, Finn Allen taps it to the off side and scampers across for a single.
FOUR! A streaky boundary! This is full and on middle, Finn Allen looks to slog-sweep it, but gets a top edge and the ball goes one bounce into the fine leg fence for a boundary.

DROPPED AND FOUR! Hardik Pandya bowls this on a hard length and on off, shaping away, Finn Allen advances down the track and tries to slog it away, but gets an outside edge towards the keeper. However, the ball keeps rising and Ishan Kishan behind the stumps leaps up, but only manages to get his outstretched right glove to it as the ball races to the third man fence for a boundary.

Slower through the air, on middle, Devon Conway goes for the pull shot, but is through the shot early. The ball takes the top edge and goes over the keeper as the fielder from short fine leg runs and collects it. Two runs taken!
Tossed up, full and on leg, Devon Conway defends it to the leg side.
Angles this one into the batter, on middle, straightens a bit, Devon Conway knocks it back to the bowler.
Another short delivery, outside off, Devon Conway pushes it towards covers.
Short again and on off, Devon Conway moves back and punches it wide of long off for a couple of runs.
Turn straightaway! Washington Sundar begins with a floated delivery, short and on off, turning away, Devon Conway sways his bat away from it at the last moment.
Washington Sundar to operate from the other end.
This is on a hard length, in the channel outside off, Finn Allen gets behind the line of it and blocks it on the pitch.
Short and on the leg stump line, Devon Conway pulls it towards fine leg for one.
FOUR! Devon Conway gets off the mark in style! Hardik Pandya pitches this up, on the pads, Devon Conway stays there and whips it towards the vacant deep mid-wicket fence for a boundary.
Back of a length and on leg, Devon Conway looks to flick it away, but misses and gets hit on the pads as the ball rolls towards the bowler.
Hardik Pandya serves this fuller and around off, angling away, Devon Conway leaves it alone.
Finn Allen and New Zealand are underway straightaway! Hardik Pandya starts with a short-of-a-length delivery, on leg, Finn Allen pulls it towards deep backward square leg for a single.

All in readiness for the play to begin! The umpires and the Indian players are already out in the middle. Devon Conway and Finn Allen are the openers for New Zealand. And, as seen in recent times, skipper Hardik Pandya will take the new ball. Let's play...

Washington Sundar is in for a quick chat. He says that there are different plans for different batters but he focuses on keeping things simple. Adds that in the Powerplay there are two fielders outside and tries to bowl according to his field. Tells that he has worked on his batting in the last year or so and is able to get more information as he is batting in various situations.

Hardik Pandya, the captain of India says that would have batted first as well but says bowling is also fine. Adds that this is a new team and they are learning from these games. Tells that it cannot get difficult than this in a bilateral series. Mentions that they need to improve as a bowling unit and do the basic rights and try to enjoy the game as much as possible. Informs that Yuzvendra Chahal is playing and 'Kul-Cha' is back together after a long time.

Mitchell Santner, the skipper of New Zealand says that they will have a bat first as the stats suggest it is difficult to chase here. Adds that after the ODI series, it was good to get a win. Mentions that it is never easy beating India at home and the best way to slow them down is by taking wickets. Adds that yes, it is a big ground and will look to use the dimensions well. Informs that they have gone with the same playing XI.

India (Playing XI) - Ishan Kishan (WK), Shubman Gill, Rahul Tripathi, Suryakumar Yadav, Hardik Pandya (C), Deepak Hooda, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav, Shivam Mavi, Yuzvendra Chahal (In for Umran Malik), Arshdeep Singh.

New Zealand (Unchanged Playing XI) - Finn Allen, Devon Conway (WK), Mark Chapman, Glenn Phillips, Daryl Mitchell, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (C), Ish Sodhi, Jacob Duffy, Lockie Ferguson, Blair Tickner.
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of Mitchell Santner. New Zealand have elected to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Danny Morrison is pitchside. He says that it is one of the bigger grounds going around in India and says that it is 76 meters straight. Ajit Agarkar joins him and says that there's a tacky look to it and there's red soil underneath which means there will be some purchase for the spinners. Mentions that the side batting second will be hoping for a bit of dew as it is the easiest pitch for batting.

New Zealand, on the other hand put in their best performance of the series in the first T20I and finally got their first win of the tour. They used the conditions perfectly in their favour and outplayed the home side. Devon Conway and Finn Allen will be key at the top order again. Their pace attack is a weakened one and the onus will be on Lockie Ferguson but the spin arsenal looks solid. This game will be played on a pitch which usually is suitable for batting and it will interesting to see how the Kiwis line up for this one. They will hope to continue the momentum and seal the series with a game to spare. Let's see who comes out on top. Toss and team news in a bit.

India came into this series with a young and not-so-experienced squad which showed in their performance. The positive for them was the all-round performance from Washington Sundar. They could not read the conditions in the previous game and looked a bit under-prepared against spin. With Shubman Gill and Arshdeep Singh both unable to find form in the T20I format, there might be a case for Prithvi Shaw and Mukesh Kumar but it remains to be seen whether India would take that gamble in a must-win game. The Men in Blue will look to execute their plans better and level the series in this game.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the 2nd T20I between India and New Zealand. India’s unbeaten record in T20I bilatreal series is under threat after New Zealand pulled the final straw in the 1st T20I at Ranchi to hand over a 21-run defeat. The second and now the pretty important T20I will be played at Bharat Ratna Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ekana Cricket Stadium in Lucknow. Both sides will look for a win but for different reasons.
... MATCH DAY ...

The caravan moves to Lucknow for the second T20I of the 3-match T20I series between India and New Zealand. Having emerged victorious at Ranchi in the first T20I, the visitors hold a 1-0 lead heading into the second T20I at the Bharat Ratna Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ekana Cricket Stadium. New Zealand will be hoping to take an unassailable 2-0 lead with a win in Lucknow, whereas India will look to bounce back with a win in the second T20I and take the series to a decider in Ahmedabad. Having been sent into bat first in the first T20I, New Zealand were off to a flying start but lost their way as India fought back with some quick wickets. However, Daryl Mitchell helped New Zealand recover and reach a challenging total with a quickfire knock. In their pursuit of 177, India got off to a shaky start and kept losing wickets at regular intervals. Washington Sundar did show some late resistance, but it was not enough to help the hosts get over the line. India’s pace attack had an off day in the first T20I, with Arshdeep Singh being the most expensive, going for 51 runs from his four overs. The hosts might look to bolster the seam attack by bringing in the uncapped Mukesh Kumar. In the batting department, they have the option of bringing in Prithvi Shaw to provide solidity at the top of the order. On the other hand, New Zealand looked settled in the first T20I and might stick with the same team. Will New Zealand seal the series in Lucknow, or will India force a series decider? We shall find out together.
